sections.h2: Which Allen County, KY offices deal with my property tax?
sections.html:
Allen County splits property tax between a valuation office and a collector. The Property Valuation Administrator sets what each parcel is worth, and the Allen County Sheriff sends out and collects the bills. The PVA does not decide how much tax you pay and does not collect it. Your bill is the assessed value multiplied by rates set by the county, the school board and districts such as the library and health department.

  • PVA: 201 W Main St #1, Scottsville, KY 42164. Phone (270) 237-3711. Open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday.
  • Sheriff (tax collector): 194 W Wood St, Scottsville, KY 42164. Phone (270) 237-3210. The sheriff's page has a tax bill search.
  • New owners who did not receive a bill can call the Sheriff's Office at 270-237-3388, a number the PVA's page gives for that purpose.

Kentucky law sets the assessment date at January 1, and ownership for tax purposes is fixed by that same date. If you buy a house after January 1, the bill for that year is issued in the former owner's name. The PVA tries to mail the new owner a copy using the recorded deed.

sections.h2: How much extra does an unpaid Allen County tax bill cost?
sections.html:
The cost climbs in steps once the sheriff hands the bill to the county clerk. The Department of Revenue illustrates it with a $1,000 bill: the certificate of delinquency starts at $1,254.00 after a 10 percent penalty, the sheriff's add-on fee and an assumed 4 percent sheriff's commission. From there interest of 1 percent a month and commissions for the clerk and the county attorney are added.

State example of a $1,000 bill after transfer to the county clerk (source: Kentucky Department of Revenue)
When paidTotal due
Within five business days of transfer$1,387.79
After the county attorney's first notice$1,611.30
In May, second month of interest$1,627.61
After newspaper advertising in June$1,659.90
At the tax sale, paid by a third-party purchaser$1,704.21

The state's figures use assumed rates, and the sheriff's actual commission governs a real bill. Ask the Allen County Sheriff for a written payoff before closing so the title company has an exact number.

sections.h2: What are the tax payment windows in Allen County?
sections.html:
Bills follow the schedule in KRS 134.015. Paying in full by November 1 gets a 2 percent discount on the amount otherwise due. The face amount is due from November 2 to December 31, a 5 percent penalty is added during January, and a 10 percent penalty applies after that.

The sheriff collects until April 15. At the close of business that day, every unpaid bill moves to the county clerk, a lien is recorded against the parcel, and the bill is now called a certificate of delinquency. At least 90 days must pass before a tax sale, and the sale must come within 135 days of the transfer. The county attorney mails notices in between, and the clerk advertises the list 30 to 45 days before the sale.

A lien from a delinquent bill follows the land. Under KRS 134.015(5) it lasts until the taxes are paid or 11 years pass under KRS 134.420, whoever owns the property. A buyer cannot walk away from it, so sellers with a balance should clear it or have it paid from proceeds.

sections.h2: How do I contest an Allen County assessment?
sections.html:
Begin with the PVA office, because the state requires a conference with the PVA or a deputy before any appeal. The real property tax roll is open to inspection for 13 days starting the first Monday in May, and the PVA must advertise those dates in the newspaper with the largest circulation.

After the conference, file the appeal with the county clerk by the close of business on the workday after the inspection period ends. The local board of assessment appeals, made up of county property owners, meets 25 to 35 days after inspection closes. Come with proof of value, such as photos of condition, repair estimates, insurance records and nearby sales. The board decides only on evidence presented while both you and the PVA's representative are in the room, and it must give a written reason for any change.

Taxpayers may record the hearing on audio. If bills are printed before your appeal is decided, the bill uses your stated opinion of value, and a supplemental bill follows if the board lands higher.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the Kentucky homestead exemption in Allen County?
sections.html:
Homeowners 65 or older, and owners classified as totally disabled, can claim it. For the 2025 and 2026 assessment years the exemption is $49,100, and it is taken off the home's assessed value before the tax rates are applied. A $192,300 house, the Census median for Allen County, would be taxed on $143,200.

The application is filed with the Allen County PVA at (270) 237-3711. A disability claim based on a federal or Kentucky Retirement Systems finding of permanent total disability does not need to be renewed each year, and neither does one by a veteran with a service-connected disability. Other disability claims must be renewed annually.

sections.h2: What should I know about Allen County, Kentucky, before selling?
sections.html:
Allen County lies on the Tennessee line in south central Kentucky and was formed in 1815 from parts of Barren and Warren counties. Scottsville is the county seat and its only city. The county is part of the Bowling Green metropolitan area, and its neighbors are Warren, Barren, Monroe and Simpson counties in Kentucky and Macon and Sumner counties in Tennessee. A courthouse fire in 1902 destroyed some county records, which can complicate very old title research.

Allen County has added residents steadily. The Census Bureau counted 20,588 residents in 2020 and estimated 22,536 in 2025, an increase of 9.5 percent.

  • Housing units: 9,390.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 74.5 percent.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $192,300.
  • Median household income: $61,403, with 14.3 percent of people in poverty.
  • Mean commute: 27.3 minutes, against 23.8 minutes in neighboring Adair County.
  • Building permits in 2025: 17.

With only 17 permits in a county of more than 9,000 housing units, most sales are of existing houses. A seller who has the tax account paid up and a clean deed of record faces fewer questions at closing.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Allen County, Kentucky?
faqs.a: The Allen County Sheriff collects it, under KRS 134.140 and 160.500. The office is at 194 W Wood St in Scottsville and its number is (270) 237-3210. The PVA only assesses the value of the property.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Allen County taxes late?
faqs.a: Five percent in January and 10 percent after January 31, on top of the face amount. After April 15 the clerk adds interest of 1 percent per month plus commissions and fees, as shown in the state's examples.

faqs.q: Is the Allen County homestead exemption automatic at age 65?
faqs.a: No. You must apply through the Allen County PVA. Once approved it generally continues for as long as you own and live in the home. The amount is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, set by the Kentucky Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: I bought a house in Allen County after January 1. Who gets the tax bill?
faqs.a: The bill for that year goes out in the former owner's name, because ownership for tax purposes is fixed on January 1. The PVA tries to mail a copy to the new owner. If none arrives, the sheriff can supply it.

faqs.q: Can an Allen County tax lien block a sale?
faqs.a: It can complicate one. The lien stays on the property until paid or until 11 years pass under KRS 134.420, regardless of ownership. Get a payoff from the sheriff and settle it at or before closing.
